done_when: The refusal explains that the roadmap entry is needed for the story to be created from the fix, and that it goes on the fix's own branch.

known.title: Refusal gives the wrong reason for using the fix branch

findings.body:
Gain 3, Work 1, Harm 3
Raise: Functional
Case: normal use - A fix has unmerged changes and its roadmap entry is added only on the fix branch.
The refusal says the story is made from the fix's branch, so a reader can expect those changes and the entry in the new story worktree. The coordinator note specifies this explanation, but does not account for `story.py:145-146`, which starts the story branch from the default branch, and `story.py:1141-1144`, which renames the fix branch into the first task instead. The refusal should explain that the task carries the entry.
findings.title: Refusal gives the wrong reason for using the fix branch

findings.body:
Gain 3, Work 1, Harm 3
Raise: Test
Case: normal use - Promotion is refused because the fix has no roadmap entry.
The new assertion checks only that the output says the story is made from the fix's branch. The test would still pass if the refusal omitted that an entry is needed before the story can start, or directed the entry to the default worktree: its other assertions do not check either statement. Extend this command-level test to cover both required details.
findings.title: Gate: tests/test_story_without_a_spec.py::test_5_promotion_keeps_its_existing_roadmap_route

stop.reason: One more round (owner): the reason in the sentence came from the coordinator's wrong note

why: After a story is made from a fix, the refusal for a missing roadmap entry asks for the entry to be committed on the fix's branch without saying why, so people expect to add it on the default branch.
